payload.description:
**Phase 1 of 7. Decide before writing more code against the current name.**

- **Blocked by:** a human naming call
- **Runs in parallel with:** nothing; everything downstream inherits the answer
- **Unblocks:** every card that says organization

---
**Three nested things, two of them currently called organization.**

| Level | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| AWS Organization | The billing container of member accounts |
| Deployment | One AWS account, one customer company, one set of stacks and hostnames |
| Tenant (`tenant_id`) | A department or team inside a deployment |

A deployment is multi-tenant within itself. The customer company is the deployment. So the tenant-level entity, currently named Organization in models.py and org_records.py, is named after the level above it.

**Recommendation: Team.** It matches how the levels are actually described, collides with neither the AWS Organization nor the customer, and holds the office metaphor together, where a deployment is the company and a tenant is a department. `tenant_id` stays the identifier in code, keys, and the worker protocol either way; only the product-facing entity name is in question.

**Cost of deciding late.** The name is in roughly twenty-six places across models.py and org_records.py plus features/organizations.feature and features/steps/organization_steps.py, all landed in #111. It grows with every phase, and phase 5 spreads it through the channel and bot models. Cheap now, expensive after phase 3.

**Done when:** the name is chosen and docs/ORGANIZATIONS.md, the Kanbus cards, and the code agree.
payload.title: Name the tenant-level entity before it spreads
